Below are the integrity rules for course enrolment records and one batch of 24 records to be checked against them. At most one rule is broken, and only in one place. A rule asks for exactly what its sentence says; whatever no listed rule covers is not a violation, however odd it looks.

Each record has these fields: enrol_id (text), student (text), starts_on (date, YYYY-MM-DD), invoice_ref (text), transfer_of (text), level (text), grant_id (text), amount_due (whole number), lab_slot (text), tuition (whole number), materials (whole number), ends_on (date, YYYY-MM-DD), module (text), needs_lab (text), list_pos (whole number).

Rules:
R1. Within the batch, all values of `enrol_id` differ from one another.
R2. Every record after the first has a `list_pos` that is one higher than that of the record just before it.
R3. `amount_due` is the sum of `tuition` and `materials`; any other stored value breaks the rule.
R4. A combination of `module` and `student` that turns up in two records is not allowed, although each of the two fields may repeat by itself.
R5. When `transfer_of` is filled in, it must be the `enrol_id` of a record that stands earlier in the batch.
R6. No record has a `ends_on` that lies before its `starts_on`; the two may coincide.
R7. `level` must be one of the following: "core", "advanced", "seminar".
R8. A record whose `needs_lab` is "yes" needs a filled-in `lab_slot`; for other records `lab_slot` is optional.
